meta.title: 5 Stoic lessons for controlling your anger

plates.query: J. M. W. Turner The Burning of the Houses of Parliament painting
ancient Roman bust of Seneca sculpture
Caspar David Friedrich calm still lake evening painting

beats.text: Five Stoic lessons for the moment anger takes hold.
One. Seneca called anger a brief madness — and warned it harms the one who holds it most.
Two. The insult is the first arrow. Your fury is the second — and only that one is yours to stop.
Three. Delay. Count to ten, then ten more. Anger rarely survives a little patience.
Four. Ask one question: is this really worth my peace of mind? The honest answer is almost never.
Five. The finest revenge, the Stoics said, is simply to be unlike the person who wronged you.
You can't always stop the spark. You can refuse to hand it the whole forest.

source_note: Inspired by Seneca's On Anger & Marcus Aurelius.
